name: e28-soak-r2-diag-logs
not_the_soak_row: This run tests a hypothesis about the cause of e28-soak-r2's failure. Whatever it shows, it is not the M4 soak row and does not replace e28-soak-r2, which stays failed.
hypothesis: The store's slow durable barriers come from writeback of the fixture's bulk logs on the store's volume, on the kernel's 31-second cycle. With those logs off the volume, the barrier tail and the slow renewals should shrink and the 31-second cycle should fade.
only_change: each tile's stdout/stderr (input-trace) log and its logs/anticheat.log are written to a tmpfs directory, /dev/shm/goliath-e28-logs-<run>, through symlinks at their usual paths; the directory is removed afterwards
unchanged_on_the_data_volume: proxy and sidecar state and logs
harness_option: --bulk-logs-tmpfs on e25-soak-control, e25-soak-cell and e24-run; default off; accepted only for names containing -diag-
memory_check: r2 wrote 3,545 MiB of these logs in about 1,290 s of tile lifetime, 2.75 MiB/s, so about 5.5 GiB for a full window. The option refuses to start below 7 GiB of free tmpfs or 9 GiB of MemAvailable. MemAvailable before and after and the tmpfs size at the end are recorded.
smoke: e28-soak-r2-diag-logs-smoke, 60 s at 425 players: all eight links intact, 296,917,804 bytes on tmpfs, every byte archived through the usual paths, directory removed
readers_checked: the native-log archive walk and the failure-evidence glob read these logs by their usual paths and follow the links; no audit reads them any other way
reported: store barriers over 50, 100, 200 and 400 ms and the maximum
renewal replies over 200 ms, the maximum and whether each installed
whether the 31-second cycle is still visible
on_failure: diagnose and report; no further variants without asking the reviewer
